correctness.rationale: For a uniformly drawn fixed-size k-subset of [n], conditional on span r the n-r choices of left endpoint have identical interior uniform C(r-1,k-2) configurations. With z=r+1-k zeros and endpoints 1, a word with h one-runs has C(k-1,h-1)C(z-1,h-2) compositions; A=k-h, and z=0 is deterministic. Uniform insertion of one zero in any of r interior gaps is a coupling because every longer word has exactly z+1 zero-deletion preimages; thus A_{r+1}<=A_r a.s. The conditional mean (k-1)(k-2)/(r-1) for k>=3, k=2 boundary, and covariance identity give strict negative Cov(A,g(R)) for 2<=k<n and strictly increasing g. Independent all-subset enumeration checked 210 (n,k,r) cases through n=11 with exact fractions, not a proof of the unrestricted n family.
residual_risks: Bounded checking corroborates examples, not unrestricted quantified mathematics.
